1zl9v1eT.content:
The gloss is set small (13px Naskh, ink-3) under its words, starting under the base's right edge and running left, as on the printed page (scan above). Only lines that carry a gloss open up (74px instead of 52px); when a gloss would run into the next one on its line it goes above its words instead (صحته and وستر here), and that line opens above too. Long glosses (p90 is 9 words) run on under the following words; past ~45% of the column they wrap to a second line. Hovering a gloss or its words inks the gloss and tints the base (120ms ease-out); no popup.
Trade-offs: always visible, zero interaction, faithful to the book, and nothing marks the matn itself, so harakat stay clean and notes, highlights and footnote refs keep the words to themselves. Costs vertical space on dense pages (25 glosses) and needs collision layout. Reading flow: the eye can skip the small grey line; harakat under the text (kasra) get 4px clear before the gloss. Needs a Display setting: Under the words / On hover (G3) / Hidden. Build cost: medium-high (measure base spans per screen row, place, detect collisions, re-place on zoom, width and resize; selection must skip gloss text).
1zl9v1eT.name: Spec note

K4GNBr4G.content:
The reader's notes sit in the left margin beyond the line numbers as short cards (2 lines, then clamped) beside the line where the note starts, like comments in a document. Several on one line collapse into the first card plus «+1 more»; hovering expands the stack, lifts the hovered card (4px, shadow, accent edge, 120ms) and tints its words. Clicking edits in place. The matn carries no mark at all. Narrow window: the cards collapse to the thin bar beside the row, and the peek opens on hover as now.
Trade-offs: notes are readable without any interaction and nothing touches the letters or harakat; the margin becomes the reader's own ḥāshiya. Needs ~230px of left margin (fine at 1280px+ with the panels closed), collision stacking down the margin, and a fallback when narrow. Risk: a busy margin pulls the eye; mitigated by ink-2 text, no fill, clamping. Build cost: medium (margin layout and stacking, in-place editor).

aEMvgICb.content:
Each gloss sits in the right (start) margin beside its line, keyed to its words by a small abjad siglum (أ ب ج …) raised after the base, like a manuscript's marginal tarr. Several glosses on a line stack and push the next line's entries down. Hovering an entry or its words tints both (120ms). The last-read mark keeps its place at the column edge; entries start past it.
Trade-offs: the matn's leading is untouched, long glosses wrap freely, and the gloss is visible without a hover. But the eye travels 40–250px per gloss, dense lines (line 5 has four) overflow onto later lines, sigla add marks to the text, and the margin it needs (≥240px) disappears in a narrow window, where it falls back to G3's card. Build cost: medium (margin layout and stacking, sigla overlay).
aEMvgICb.name: Spec note

uF37s3Yf.content:
A noted span is bracketed by two small accent corners, ⌝ at its start (top right) and ⌞ at its end (bottom left), drawn as overlays outside the letters; the margin keeps one icon per row with a count. Hovering the mark or the words tints the span and opens the peek.
Trade-offs: shows exactly which words a note covers without underlines (kasra-safe) and without a chat bubble on the text; quiet enough for reading. The note text still needs a hover. Corners can meet a highlight band's edge and a footnote ref. Build cost: low (two overlays per note span, existing margin mark).
